newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Premier plans talks with Discovery.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Premier plans talks with Discovery.

text.p: Premier Oil Plc said it would hold talks later this week with executives of Perth-based petroleum producer and explorer Discovery Petroleum NL.
Discovery has rejected a 70 cent per share takeover bid by Premier as unacceptable.

The British company also said that it believed the independent experts' report commissioned by Discovery took an overly optimistic view of Discovery's exploration potential and the report's valuation of the shares relied heavily on exploration assets which may not be put into production.

"We will be continuing discussions with Peter Jones and Eric Streitberg later this week and we also intend meeting them in Perth early next week," Premier Oil Australia Pty Ltd director Stephen Lowden said in a statement.
Jones is the chairman of Discovery and Streitberg is managing director.
Discovery said on October 21 that the bid was inadequate and below the 77 to 95 cent range contained in the independent valuation prepared by merchant bank Grant Samuel.
Discovery shares ended one cent higher at 80 cents on Wednesday.

In its rejection statement, Discovery said Oil Search Ltd had paid 75 cents per share for a 10.1 percent stake since the bid was announced and that its shares had consistently traded above the offer price.
The Premier bid values Discovery at A$91.18 million based on its 130.26 million shares outstanding.
Premier said in response to the formal rejection that it would make another announcement in due course.
